Regio-, Stereo-, and Enantioselective Copper-Catalyzed Allylation of
Sulfinylamines with Allenes
Jie Zhu, Yue Zhao, Shengming Ma,* and Minyan Wang*
Abstract: Sulfinamides, pivotal scaffolds in modern organic synthesis, have undergone a continuous evolution of synthetic
methodologies over the past century, yet the precise construction of sulfur stereocenters remains a significant synthetic
challenge. Herein, we report a versatile catalytic asymmetric strategy for the synthesis of S-chirogenic allyl sulfinamides
through the direct allylation of sulfinylamines with allenes. Our methodology employs a catalytic system comprising copper
salts, hydrosilanes, and readily accessible chiral ligands, which facilitates the in situ generation of organocopper surrogates
via hydrocupration of allenes. This approach demonstrates remarkable substrate scope and excellent regio-, stereo-, and
enantioselectivity across a diverse array of sulfinamide products. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations, including
detailed experimental studies and computational analyses, have been conducted to elucidate the reaction pathway and
identify the key factors governing enantioselectivity.
Chiral sulfinamides featuring stereogenic S(IV) centers have
garnered particular attention as pivotal synthetic targets.<sup>[1–15]</sup>
These compounds not only function as crucial intermediates
for the stereoselective assembly of sulfur-containing func-
tional groups<sup>[16–19]</sup> but also exhibit remarkable versatility
as bifunctional reagents under mild photoredox catalysis
conditions.<sup>[20,21]</sup> Among these, the synthesis of chiral S-
allyl sulfinamides has garnered significant attention due to
their intricate structural complexity and diverse applications.
A landmark achievement in 1990 facilitated the enantiop-
ure synthesis of S-allyl sulfinamides via ene reactions of
trans-alkenes with N-sulfinylcarbamates derived from chiral
alcohols (Figure 1a).<sup>[22]</sup> To eliminate the reliance on chiral
auxiliaries, Beyah and colleagues in 2017 pioneered an
asymmetric catalytic variant, employing a chiral antimony
catalyst in the ene-type sulfinamidation of cis- alkenes
(Figure 1b).<sup>[23]</sup> However, the propensity of the N-sulfonyl
sulfur-centered chirality, highlighting the necessity for more
robust sulfinamide moiety to act as a leaving group, has
limited its utility in adaptable synthetic methodologies.
Sulfinylamines (R–NSO), distinguished by their orthogo-
nal cumulative π-systems, have emerged as pivotal building
blocks in organic synthesis, facilitating a diverse range of
chemical transformations.<sup>[24,25]</sup> The nucleophilic addition of
magnesium reagents to sulfinylamines, developed in 1974,
offers a direct method for synthesizing S-allyl sulfinamides, as
well as a broad range of other sulfinamides (Figure 1c).<sup>[26–28]</sup>

compatibility with sensitive functional groups by employing
readily accessible alkyl<sup>[29,30]</sup> and aryl<sup>[31]</sup> feedstocks in addition
reactions. The advent of asymmetric catalysis utilizing aryl
boron compounds<sup>[32,33]</sup> or halides<sup>[34–37]</sup> with sulfinylamines
has introduced novel pathways for the synthesis of chiral
sulfinamides. Inspired by these developments, we propose an

present an asymmetric catalytic allylation of sulfinylamines

excellent regio-, stereo-, and enantioselectivity (Figure 1d).

tioselectivity. A particularly significant advancement was
achieved in the successful transformation of 1,1-disubstituted
allenes 29a–37a featuring methyl and aryl moieties, which
afforded products 29b–37b with an exceptional enantiose-
lectivity and Z/E selectivity. To unambiguously determine
the stereochemical outcome, we performed X-ray crystal-
lographic analysis on product 34b,<sup>[71]</sup> which conclusively
established its E,R-configuration. Expanding the substrate
scope further, we demonstrated the exceptional chemoselec-
tivity of the reaction towards naphthyl (38a), long-chain alkyl
(39a), and cyclic (40a) allenes, which exclusively yielded the
desired products 38b–40b under the optimized conditions.

In conclusion, this study establishes a robust and versatile
copper-catalyzed platform for the stereoselective synthesis
of chiral S-allyl sulfinamides, addressing a long-standing
challenge in asymmetric sulfur chemistry. The developed
methodology demonstrates remarkable functional group tol-
erance and substrate scope, enabling the efficient coupling
of diverse allenes with sulfinylamines under mild reductive
conditions. Through a synergistic combination of experi-
mental investigations and computational analyses, we have
elucidated the intricate reaction mechanism and identified
key factors governing the selective aryl addition processes.
Given the growing recognition of chiral S-stereogenic com-
pounds as privileged structural motifs in pharmaceutical
development and agrochemical innovation, we anticipate
that this catalytic system will find broad applications in the
synthesis of biologically active molecules.
